entry.title: Update PlayCanvas guides for engine 2.x and the current Editor
entry.content:
Description

Updates the three PlayCanvas pages under Games > 3D on the web for PlayCanvas engine 2.x and the current Editor, and replaces all Editor screenshots.

Motivation

The pages were written for a much older engine and Editor. The engine tutorial loads a non-module build, uses the legacy model component, and links to a download URL that serves an outdated build. The Editor tutorial describes a UI that no longer exists. Readers following either one today hit outdated or broken steps.

Additional details

  • Engine tutorial: loads PlayCanvas 2.24.2 as an ES module (import map or npm), switches to render components, handles canvas resizing, adds an optional WebGPU section, and fixes the live samples. Both samples were tested in Chrome with WebGL 2 and WebGPU.
  • Editor tutorial: steps rewritten for the current Editor. All screenshots were recaptured from a real run-through and compressed with filecheck --save-compression; the outdated login and project-page images are removed.
  • Overview pages: mention WebGL 2/WebGPU, the MIT license, CDN/npm usage, and the React and Web Components wrappers; links updated.

Disclosure: I work on PlayCanvas.

entry.title: docs(html): clarify cancel event behavior on file input (#46622)
entry.content:
Description

Clarify that the cancel event on <input type=file> / HTMLInputElement fires when the user dismisses the file picker dialog without choosing a file, rather than when re-selecting the previously selected file.

Motivation

The documentation previously stated that the cancel event fires both when the dialog is cancelled and when the user re-selects the same files that were previously selected. Under the WHATWG HTML specification (§4.10.5.1.18 File Upload state), selecting a file is an affirmative selection action rather than a cancellation. In modern browsers, reselecting the identical file either fires change or does not fire a change event, but does not fire cancel. The cancel event is only fired when the user aborts or dismisses the file selection dialog without selecting files.

Additional details

  • WHATWG HTML Standard: File Upload state (§4.10.5.1.18)
  • Fixes #46622

entry.title: Remove unsupported fangsong keyword from font-family and <generic-family>
entry.content:
Description

Removes the bare fangsong keyword from the font-family page (syntax block, values list, and the live example) and from the <generic-family> page (values list and the syntax line).

Motivation

No browser treats fangsong as a generic family keyword. It only does something on systems that happen to have a font named "FangSong" installed (Windows does), so the live example falls back to the default font everywhere else. The current spec doesn't have a bare fangsong keyword either. CSS Fonts 4 now uses generic(fangsong), which no browser supports yet, so I left that out too.

BCD already dropped fangsong, kai, khmer-mul and nastaliq from css.properties.font-family (mdn/browser-compat-data#29246), so these pages were the last place still listing it.

Additional details

  • None of the engines has it in their generic family keyword list: Chromium css_value_keywords.json5, WebKit CSSValueKeywords.in, and Gecko's GenericFontFamily enum in servo/components/style/values/computed/font.rs all stop at serif, sans-serif, cursive, fantasy, monospace, system-ui and math.
  • In Chrome 156, el.style.fontFamily = '"fangsong"' reads back as fangsong (no quotes), while "serif" and "math" keep their quotes. So Chrome parses it as an ordinary family name, not a keyword.
  • CSS Fonts 4 changes list: "Consistently use generic(fangsong) instead of fangsong, as the generic font family name."

entry.title: Add missing bfcache blocking reasons from the HTML spec
entry.content:
Description

Adds the bfcache blocking reasons that are in the HTML spec but missing from MDN, and makes the NotRestoredReasonDetails.reason page point to the full list.

Motivation

The reason page only showed three examples of user agent-specific reasons, so readers had no way to find values like sharedworker-message. The guide already has a full list, but it was missing five values the spec defines:

  • rtc-used-with-cache-control-no-store
  • sharedworker-message
  • sharedworker-with-no-active-client
  • websocket-used-with-cache-control-no-store
  • webtransport-used-with-cache-control-no-store

I added those to the guide, plus the spec's note under sharedworker saying browsers can report the two more specific shared worker reasons instead. I didn't copy the whole list onto the reason page. It links to the guide section instead, so there's one list to keep in sync.

Additional details

Spec list: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#nrr-details-struct

The shared worker values came from whatwg/html#12086.

I compared the reason strings in the spec source with the list in the guide, and they now match (52 values each). markdownlint-cli2, prettier -c and cspell pass on both files. I also built both pages with rari build and checked that the new links and the #user-agent_specific_blocking_reasons anchor resolve.

entry.content:
Title: [Technical review] Add WebDriver Classic Delete Session and Status pages

Description

Added pages for the following commands of the Sessions chapter of WebDriver Classic:

  • Delete Session
  • Status

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#delete-session
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#status

Compat quirks worth looking into:

Chrome

  • Delete Session with an unknown session ID. Deleting a session that had already been deleted, or one with an ID that never existed, returned 200 with {"value":null} in my test run, where the spec returns invalid session id. BCD shows Delete Session as supported since Chrome 65 with no note.
  • Outdated w3c note. BCD's Chrome entries for both commands say to include {"goog:chromeOptions": {"w3c": true}} in the capabilities. My test sessions didn't set it, and both commands returned W3C responses.

/cc @sadym-chromium for the BCD update.

entry.title: docs(http): document multiple space-separated values for CSP sandbox directive
entry.content:
Description

Clarify that the Content-Security-Policy: sandbox directive accepts zero or more space-separated tokens to lift specific restrictions, and provide an example demonstrating multiple values.

Motivation

The syntax section previously stated that <value> could optionally be "one of the following values", which could be interpreted as permitting only a single token at a time. In the CSP specification (both CSP Level 2 and Level 3), sandbox accepts space-separated tokens, similar to the iframe sandbox attribute. This change aligns the syntax description and adds an example with multiple values.

Additional details

  • W3C Content Security Policy Level 3 – Sandbox directive

entry.title: Add note about function length where param optionality differs
entry.content: 3 years ago I asked https://github.com/orgs/mdn/discussions/201. It never got a decisive conclusion. I decided it's not worth formally defining and MDN should be free to define optionality however the readers would perceive it. However, we should document the methods' length where its value is not derived from our notion of optionality, because that's actually an observable part of its behavior.

entry.title: SVGTransform: note that browsers return SVGMatrix and fix the setMatrix() example
entry.content:
Description

The SVGTransform.matrix page now has a note that browsers return an SVG 1.1 SVGMatrix rather than a DOMMatrix, using the same wording style as the SVGRect note on the getBBox() page. On the setMatrix() page, the parameter no longer says "a live DOMMatrix", there's a note that Chromium only accepts an SVGMatrix, and the example creates its matrix with createSVGMatrix() instead of new DOMMatrix().

Motivation

The setMatrix() example throws in Chrome with TypeError: Failed to execute 'setMatrix' on 'SVGTransform': parameter 1 is not of type 'SVGMatrix'. The matrix page says the value is a DOMMatrix, but transform.matrix instanceof DOMMatrix is false, and the object has no m11, is2D, or multiplySelf(), so code written against DOMMatrix breaks.

Additional details

I ran the examples from both pages in Chrome 157. The matrix examples work as written. The old setMatrix() example throws the error above, and with createSVGMatrix() it logs SVGMatrix { a: 1, b: 0, c: 0, d: 1, e: 50, f: 50 }.

I couldn't run Firefox or Safari here, so for those I went by their IDL. Gecko's SVGTransform.webidl and WebKit's SVGTransform.idl both declare readonly attribute SVGMatrix matrix with a separate SVGMatrix interface, and their setMatrix() takes a DOMMatrix2DInit, so a DOMMatrix or plain object works there. Blink uses SVGMatrix for both, with a TODO to move to DOMMatrix: https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/a973c71e533a3e968b4849d69d730f8f97c17c2d/third_party/blink/renderer/core/svg/svg_transform.idl#L38-L43

entry.title: Update pushState() and replaceState() rate limiting behavior
entry.content:
Description

The SecurityError entries on the pushState() and replaceState() pages said the error is thrown when the method is called too frequently. This updates both pages to say the call is ignored in that case, and that some browsers still throw.

Motivation

whatwg/html#12492 (merged in June) changed the spec so rate-limited calls return early instead of throwing. Chrome and Firefox already behave that way, so readers could end up writing a try...catch for an error those browsers never throw.

Additional details

  • Chrome returns early from History::StateObjectAdded when its navigation rate limiter says no, and logs a console warning. No exception.
  • Firefox stopped throwing in Firefox 157 (bug 1922677).
  • Safari still throws a SecurityError ("Attempt to use history.pushState() more than ... times per ... seconds" in WebKit's History.cpp), tracked in https://webkit.org/b/317129.

The go(), back(), forward(), Location.assign() and Location.replace() pages already say the call may be ignored, so I left those alone.
